_description: Merge rules for Phase 1 product families that share an EHI export URL. Products sharing a URL start as separate families (step 2). This file encodes step 3 decisions: which to merge based on content investigation, and which to keep separate despite sharing a URL. Products NOT mentioned here remain as standalone families.
_methodology: Each rule covers one (developer, URL) group. 'families' defines the merged groupings. Products listed together in one family share a documented EHI approach. Products in separate families have distinct approaches. If a product from the URL group is not listed in any family here, it stays as its own standalone family (i.e., no merge).

merges.rationale: EHI Export Documentation accordion has 5 separate product-level doc sets. Paragon EHR and Paragon Denali share one FHIR Capability Statement. Sunrise Acute, Ambulatory, and Hospital-based share one HTML tree export definition. TouchWorks has its own HTML tree definition (stays standalone since it's only 1 product).

families.name: E*HealthLine EHR
products: CARE© Integrated Hospital Information Management System

merges.rationale: Single EHI Tables export with unified TSV schema covering all products.

Single EHI export page documents 2 configurations that apply across all products depending on site deployment. Config 1 (eChart/FHIR/C-CDA) covers Expanse, 6.15, and some older platforms in acute mode. Config 2 (CSV/FHIR/C-CDA) covers older platforms. Both configs documented together as one vendor approach.

Both products are 'athenaClinicals' variants (one adds 'for Hospitals and Health Systems'). JS-rendered page could not be fully verified, but product name overlap and shared URL strongly suggest shared approach.

families.name: athenaClinicals

merges.rationale: Page explicitly states 'athenaPractice and athenaFlow support the export of electronic health information (EHI)' and documents a shared FHIR R4 + custom resource approach.

no_merge.rationale: Page shows separate product sections with separate certifications, costs, and RWT plans. No EHI-specific documentation visible on page to confirm shared approach. Keep separate.
Each product has its own EHI documentation subpage (/ehi-all-data-myavatar, /ehi-all-data-myevolv, /ehi-all-data-myunity, /ehi-all-data-theraoffice). Separate EHI approaches per product.

Page documents completely different approaches: Enterprise EHR has a native database dictionary with 200+ tables; Office exports CCDA+CSV+binary. Also lists Direct Messaging (CDA) and Mirth Connect (XML) but those are not Phase 1.
Separate EHI documentation sets: Veradigm EHR has a single PDF (v1); Veradigm View has versioned HTML documentation (up to v6). Completely different export approaches and documentation quality.
